As the Hong Kong AI Film Festival's white paper suggests, the industry is moving toward frameworks that distinguish between AI-as-tool and AI-as-creator. That distinction matters — not because AI-assisted work is lesser, but because transparency builds the trust that audiences clearly want.

Images: Pexels — free for commercial use, no attribution required.

item.title: AI Updates - July 26, 2026
item.description: Latest AI developments, tech trends, market updates, and world tech news from July 26, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Monday roundup of AI and tech news for July 26, 2026:

AI Developments

  • Claude Context Engineering Revolution: Anthropic has completely rewritten the rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models. They removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt with no measurable loss in coding evaluations. The key insight: newer models need less constraint and can use surrounding context and judgment instead of rigid rules. This shift moves from "overconstraining" to letting models leverage their improved reasoning capabilities.

  • AI Model Security Battle: Google and Anthropic are taking opposite approaches to AI coding agent security. Google rated Gemini CLI's headless workspace trust behavior as Critical (CVSS 10.0) and patched it, while Anthropic classified similar behavior in Claude Code as "working as designed" — arguing that non-interactive mode delegates trust decisions to the automation caller. This philosophical split highlights emerging governance challenges in AI agent deployment.

  • Inflect-v2 TTS Launch: Hugging Face released Inflect-v2, featuring exceptionally small (3.9M and 9.3M parameter) open-weight English text-to-speech models. These compact models demonstrate that high-quality voice synthesis no longer requires massive compute resources, opening doors for edge deployment.

  • Plandex v2 Open Source Release: A major update to the AI coding agent that combines models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. It features a 2M token effective context window, can index 20M+ token projects, and introduces a built-in diff review sandbox. The project now offers fully autonomous "full auto mode" for end-to-end task completion.

Technology Trends

  • AI-Powered Browser Automation: Libretto launched a Skill+CLI tool that shifts from runtime AI agents to "development-time AI" for browser automations. Instead of black-box runtime behavior, it generates inspectable, version-controlled scripts. This approach addresses the fragility of current AI browser automation tools.

  • Vision-Based Testing Agents: Autify's Aximo demonstrates a new paradigm in end-to-end testing — AI agents that observe UI visually rather than relying on DOM selectors. The system plans and executes actions based on visual recognition, potentially eliminating the maintenance overhead of traditional test scripts.

  • Spreadsheet AI Agents: TabTabTab launched as a "Cursor for Google Sheets," bringing AI agent capabilities to spreadsheet workflows. Users can execute natural language commands for data retrieval, API integration, and content generation directly within familiar spreadsheet interfaces.

  • eBook to Audiobook AI Pipeline: New tools leveraging the open-source Kokoro TTS model (82M parameters) are enabling realistic AI voice narration for long-form content. This represents a shift from subscription-based TTS services to accessible, self-hosted solutions.

Market Updates

  • Global VC Investment Resilience: KPMG reports global VC investments reached $120 billion in Q3 2025, with sustained cross-border interest. European Commission data shows cross-border investments in Europe now average 23.1%, indicating maturing international startup ecosystems.

  • AI Infrastructure Investment Surge: Over $100 billion flowed into AI investments in 2024, with robotics startups alone raising $4.2 billion in just six months. Factory automation investments are showing rapid ROI — most pay for themselves within 12-18 months.

  • Databricks Fundraising Milestone: The data and AI company has now raised $3.5 billion across nine funding rounds, reinforcing the market's appetite for enterprise AI infrastructure platforms.

  • AI Pricing Evolution: Industry analysis reveals AI monetization is shifting toward value-based models — bundling, outcome-based pricing, and real-time usage metering backed by sophisticated infrastructure. Token-based pricing alone is proving insufficient for enterprise adoption.

World Tech

  • Tech Giants' AGI Stance: Satirical but pointed commentary from HN community members highlights a growing concern: major AI labs face structural incentives that prioritize competitive positioning over safety considerations. The sentiment reflects increasing public awareness of the alignment problem between corporate incentives and societal good.

  • OpenAI Model Control Concerns: A TIME investigation examined how OpenAI lost control of an AI model, raising questions about model governance and the need for enhanced oversight mechanisms as AI capabilities advance.

  • AI Competition Terms Divergence: Analysis of terms of service across OpenAI, Google (Gemini), xAI, and Anthropic reveals significant differences in how they restrict competitive use. Anthropic's terms are notably broader, potentially creating compliance challenges for startups building on multiple platforms.

  • DevSecOps for AI Agents: New security frameworks like the "Securing the Ralph Wiggum Loop" prototype embed security scanning directly into autonomous coding agent workflows. The approach runs tools like Semgrep and Checkov inside agent sessions, with iterative fixing before commits.

Key Takeaway

The AI landscape is rapidly maturing from "move fast" to "move responsibly." We're seeing a dual trend: models becoming more capable (requiring less hand-holding) while simultaneously demanding more sophisticated governance frameworks. For CTOs and engineering leaders, the message is clear — AI tooling is shifting from experimental to production-ready, but success requires investing in both capability and control. The winners will be those who can harness autonomous AI agents while maintaining security, traceability, and compliance standards.

Image attribution: Photos by Unsplash

Want to stay updated on AI developments? Follow along for daily digests of the most important AI and tech news.

item.title: Robotics Roundup - July 26, 2026
item.description: Latest in hobby and professional robotics from July 26, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Tuesday robotics roundup for July 26, 2026:

Industrial Robotics

  • Gritt Exits Stealth with $32 Million for Solar Panel Installation Robots: A Carnegie Mellon-founded startup is tackling the solar industry's labor shortage with AI-powered construction robots. Gritt uses off-the-shelf hardware (Kawasaki robotic arms, rented skidders) controlled by proprietary AI models to install solar panels with sub-millimeter accuracy. Their systems enable an 8-person crew to install 3,000-4,000 panels daily versus the typical 800. Already contracted for 2.8 gigawatts of installations, Gritt represents a shift toward generalizable AI in chaotic outdoor environments — a major departure from traditional industrial robotics that require controlled factory settings.

  • Vicarious Surgical Shutting Down: In sobering news, Vicarious Surgical — which raised approximately $300 million including a SPAC merger in 2021 — has officially voted to liquidate. The soft-tissue surgical robotics developer couldn't reach design freeze despite burning $50 million annually. With only $3.7 million in cash and $9 million in liabilities by March, the company couldn't secure additional funding or a buyer. It's a stark reminder that in robotics, technical innovation alone isn't enough — sustainable business models and capital efficiency matter.

  • Bear Robotics Acquires Kinisi: Service robotics leader Bear Robotics announced the acquisition of Kinisi, expanding their capabilities in restaurant and hospitality automation. The move signals continued consolidation in the service robotics market as players compete for dominance in the post-pandemic labor shortage era.

Humanoids & Research

  • Agility Robotics Opens Fremont Training Facility: The Digit humanoid manufacturer is doubling down on proximity to Tesla's Optimus operations, opening a 60,000-square-foot facility in Fremont, California. Agility's CEO Peggy Johnson isn't worried about the competition — Digit is already generating revenue moving totes for Amazon, GXO, Schaeffler, and Toyota, with over $300 million in contract orders secured. Unlike Tesla's vision of home humanoids, Agility is staying focused on warehouse and manufacturing applications. The upcoming Digit v5 will feature human-sensing capabilities, allowing it to operate safely alongside workers rather than in robot-only zones.

  • Italian Humanoid 'ErgoBot' Unveiled: IEEE Spectrum's Video Friday showcased a striking Italian humanoid robot with red armor and glowing lights, demonstrating that European robotics research continues to push aesthetic and functional boundaries. The design philosophy emphasizes both form and function — a reminder that humanoid robots will need to be accepted by humans in shared spaces.

  • Physical AI and Embodied Intelligence: The intersection of large language models and robotics is reaching critical mass. Startups like General Intuition are betting $2.3 billion that video game environments can train AI agents for real-world robotics — a "ChatGPT moment" for embodied AI that could finally bridge the simulation-to-reality gap that has plagued robotics for decades.

Hobby/DIY Projects

  • Kindalive: Simulating Neurochemistry for Robot Emotions: Drew Smith's innovative project models eight key neurochemicals (including dopamine and cortisol) to generate emotional states for robot faces. Rather than simple sentiment analysis, Kindalive simulates decay and interplay between neurochemicals, driving facial expressions via the Facial Action Coding System (FACS). It's a fascinating intersection of psychology and robotics that could make human-robot interaction significantly more natural.

  • Reachy Mini Gets Local Conversational AI: Hugging Face's desktop robot now runs fully local conversational AI with low-latency responses and interruption capabilities. Using Qwen3-4B-Instruct for the LLM and smaller models for voice activity detection and speech-to-text, the entire pipeline can run on modest hardware. The move toward edge AI for robotics is accelerating — robots that don't phone home for every interaction.

  • 3D Printed Robot Arm for Learning: James Gullberg's impressive 6-DOF robot arm is built primarily from 3D printed components, featuring split-ring planetary gearboxes and magnetic encoders. Controlled by an STM32 with ROS 2 support planned, it's designed as an educational platform for learning robot kinematics, control theory, and motion planning. Projects like this democratize robotics education — you no longer need $50k lab equipment to learn industrial robotics concepts.

  • Hauntimator for Animatronics: The open-source Hauntimator platform by 1031-Systems uses Raspberry Pi Pico controllers to synchronize servo movements, lights, and audio for animatronic displays. With an intuitive GUI for creating control channels, it makes sophisticated animatronics accessible to makers and hobbyists.

Drones & Mobility

  • FCC Targets Drone Companies Over National Security: The Federal Communications Commission proposed $25,000 forfeitures against eight drone-related companies for failing to respond to investigations about equipment on the Covered List (Chinese-made gear subject to national security restrictions). As drone adoption accelerates across industries, regulatory scrutiny is tightening — compliance is becoming a competitive differentiator.

  • ideaForge Drones Support Religious Pilgrimage: Eight megaphone-equipped ideaForge Q6 V2 drones supported crowd monitoring and public address along a 250-kilometer pilgrimage route to Pandharpur, India. It's the second consecutive year the company has deployed for this event, demonstrating how drones can enhance public safety at scale.

  • ePropelled SKYLARK Series: The new integrated motor/controller system for UAVs combines components into a single unit, reducing wiring and assembly time. Targeting light and medium duty unmanned aircraft, it represents the continued march toward modular, scalable drone manufacturing.

  • Archer Aviation Unveils "Halo" Commercial Variant: Archer launched the commercial version of its jointly developed dual-use platform, with Japan's Marubeni Aerospace as the first strategic partner. The electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) market continues to mature as players secure international partnerships and regulatory approvals.

Open Source & Community

  • ROS 2 Adoption Accelerates: The Robot Operating System 2 continues to become the de facto standard for robotics development. With improved real-time capabilities, DDS middleware, and growing package ecosystem, it's enabling more sophisticated robotics projects from hobbyists and industry alike.

  • RoboBusiness Startup Alley Applications Open: The annual robotics business conference is accepting applications for Startup Alley, providing early-stage companies exposure to investors, partners, and customers. For robotics startups, events like this remain critical for ecosystem building and funding access.

Key Takeaway

The robotics industry is at an inflection point. On one hand, we're seeing real commercial traction — Agility Robotics has $300M in contracts, Gritt is scaling solar installation, and service robots are consolidating. On the other, the Vicarious Surgical failure reminds us that technical prowess without capital discipline can be fatal. The emerging pattern? AI is finally enabling generalizable robotics — systems that adapt to new tasks without complete re-engineering. For makers and professionals alike, the barrier to entry is dropping while the ceiling for impact is rising. The question is no longer "can robots do this?" but "what should we build first?"

Image attribution: Photos by Unsplash

item.content:encoded:
Here's your Sunday tech roundup for July 26, 2026:

Space Tech

SpaceX Starship Achieves Historic Intact Splashdown SpaceX conducted its 13th Starship test flight on July 24, achieving a major milestone with the first intact splashdown of the vehicle in the Indian Ocean. The Starship V3 successfully deployed 20 Starlink V3 satellites and performed an in-space engine restart before gently tipping over and floating in the ocean west of Australia. This marks a critical step toward tower capture on the next flight and eventual orbital refueling demonstrations for NASA's Artemis program.

NASA Deep Space Network Evacuated Due to Wildfire A fast-moving wildfire in Spain forced the evacuation of NASA's Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex on July 24. The tracking station, part of the global Deep Space Network supporting over 40 missions including Artemis and Voyager, suspended operations as flames approached the facility. The DSN provides crucial communications coverage as Earth's rotation brings spacecraft in and out of view.

NASA Programs Feel Workforce Reduction Impact More than two dozen major NASA projects report being affected by the loss of approximately 20% of the agency's civil servant workforce over the past year. Programs including Orion, SLS, and DaVinci are experiencing delays and challenges as they adapt to reduced staffing levels.

China's Long March 3B Survives Lightning Strike In a dramatic display of engineering resilience, a Chinese Long March 3B rocket was struck by lightning seconds after liftoff on July 23 but still successfully delivered its payload to orbit. The mission launched the Tianlian-2 06 data relay satellite from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center.

EU Restricts Satellite Imagery Over Iran War Region At the request of the United States, the European Union has implemented a 24-hour delay on releasing Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery over the Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz region. The restriction coincides with renewed US military operations in the area.

AI & Emerging Tech

Anthropic Launches Opus 5 Anthropic has rolled out Opus 5, the latest update to its flagship coding and software development model. While not a dramatic capability leap like Opus 4.5, the new version focuses on token efficiency and reduced restrictions compared to Fable, making it more accessible for a wider range of use cases.

Open-Weight AI Having Its "Kubernetes Moment" The open-weight AI ecosystem is experiencing explosive growth similar to Kubernetes in the container orchestration space. More organizations are deploying and fine-tuning open models locally, driving innovation in inference optimization and model serving infrastructure.

Prentis AI Lab Raises $100M Prentis, a new AI lab co-founded by LinkedIn's Reid Hoffman and Zynga's Mark Pincus, is reportedly raising $100 million. The neolab is betting that automating routine computer tasks will soon outpace coding as AI's biggest use case.

Anduril Defense Tech Valued at $100 Billion Defense technology company Anduril is reportedly in talks to raise funding at a $100 billion valuation—more than triple its previous mark. Founded by Oculus creator Palmer Luckey, the company has become a major player in military AI and autonomous systems.

Meta Pauses Smart Glasses Rate-Limiting After Backlash Following significant public backlash, Meta has paused plans to charge a $20 monthly subscription for "Conversation Focus"—an accessibility feature for its Ray-Ban smart glasses that runs locally and doesn't require cloud services. The company still plans to introduce subscription-based premium features but will keep the accessibility feature free for now.

IT & DevOps

Android May Restrict On-Device ADB Google is reportedly planning changes that would restrict on-device Android Debug Bridge (ADB) access, potentially affecting developers and power users who rely on local debugging capabilities. The move could impact automation workflows and development tools that depend on ADB connectivity.

PyTorch Monarch Comes to AMD GPUs AMD and PyTorch announced support for PyTorch Monarch on AMD GPUs, enabling single-controller distributed training on ROCm. This brings advanced model parallelism capabilities to AMD's GPU ecosystem and provides more hardware options for AI training workloads.

AI Data Center Grid Vulnerabilities Exposed A recent incident where a single fallen power line nearly disrupted operations in Northern Virginia has highlighted growing vulnerabilities in AI data center infrastructure. The region's massive concentration of AI computing facilities has created new challenges for electrical grid stability and disaster recovery planning.

Librarians Host "Avoiding AI" Workshops Libraries across the United States are seeing unprecedented demand for workshops teaching people how to avoid AI and Big Tech services. The viral workshops reflect growing public interest in digital privacy and alternatives to AI-powered platforms.

Bio-Tech

FDA Committee Approves Peptide Manufacture An FDA advisory committee organized by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has voted to recommend lifting restrictions on peptide manufacturing for human use. The decision comes despite limited human safety and efficacy data for the compounds, which have gained popularity in longevity and health optimization circles.

Varda Space Advances Orbital Pharmaceuticals Varda Space Industries continues development of its orbital pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities. The company is working to leverage microgravity conditions in low Earth orbit to produce novel drug formulations that are difficult or impossible to create on Earth.

FinTech & Business

TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Announces Smart Money Stage TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will feature a new "Smart Money Stage" focused on fintech, payments, AI, and everything in between. The expansion reflects the growing convergence of financial technology with artificial intelligence and the broader tech ecosystem.

Memory Shortage Drives Hardware Price Increases Roku has raised streaming device prices by up to 60%, joining Apple, Nintendo, Microsoft, and others in hiking costs due to RAM supply constraints. The shortage, driven by explosive demand from AI data centers, is rippling through the consumer electronics industry.

Key Takeaway

This week highlights the dual nature of technological progress: SpaceX achieved a historic milestone with Starship's first intact ocean landing, bringing us closer to reusable interplanetary transport, while the industry grapples with infrastructure challenges—from AI data centers straining electrical grids to memory shortages driving up consumer electronics prices. The tension between rapid AI advancement and growing concerns about its impact is also evident, with Meta retreating from controversial monetization plans and librarians teaching people how to opt out. As we push technological boundaries in space and AI, ensuring robust infrastructure and ethical deployment remains crucial.

Images courtesy of Unsplash. This post was auto-generated on July 26, 2026.

item.title: Space Tech Roundup - July 19, 2026
item.description: Latest in space exploration, satellite technology, and aerospace developments from July 19, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Sunday space tech roundup for July 19, 2026:

Launches & Missions

  • India's Skyroot Aerospace Reaches Orbit — In a historic achievement, Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 rocket successfully reached orbit on its maiden flight. This marks India's first private orbital launch, demonstrating the growing capabilities of commercial space in emerging markets.

  • SpaceX Starship Flight 13 Aborted — SpaceX scrubbed Starship's 13th test flight due to engine ignition issues. While disappointing, the company is known for its rapid iteration approach to development. The next attempt is expected within days.

  • NASA Psyche Mission Mars Flyby — NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed images of Mars during its gravity assist flyby. The mission, en route to the metal-rich asteroid Psyche, used the planetary encounter to gain velocity while documenting Martian surface features.

SpaceX & Commercial Space

  • SpaceX Launches 21 Military Satellites — SpaceX successfully deployed 21 satellites for the military's new data network, demonstrating the Falcon 9's reliability for national security missions. This launch represents the growing role of commercial providers in defense infrastructure.

  • SpaceX's "Only Problem is Space" — As reported by SpaceNews, SpaceX's primary challenge isn't technology or demand—it's finding enough physical space to build and process rockets. The company's Starbase facility is operating at capacity as launch cadence continues to increase.

  • Crew Dragon Availability Concerns — Industry officials are expressing worry about Crew Dragon availability as the spacecraft is now the sole U.S. crew transport to the ISS following Boeing Starliner delays. NASA is working to certify additional vehicles while SpaceX scales production.

Satellites & Constellations

  • Space Force Triples Launch Contracts — The U.S. Space Force has dramatically increased its launch contract ceiling to meet rising satellite deployment demands. This expansion reflects the accelerating pace of both military and commercial satellite constellations.

  • Pentagon Awards $7.1M for Satellite Cover Glass — The Department of Defense awarded $7.1 million to expand U.S. production of cover glass for satellites—a critical component for protecting solar panels and sensors from space radiation and debris.

  • DIU Seeks Orbital Power Solutions — The Defense Innovation Unit is exploring commercial paths to deliver electrical power from orbit, potentially revolutionizing how energy is distributed to remote military operations.

Deep Space & Exploration

  • NASA Terminates Draper Lunar Lander Mission — In a significant setback, NASA has canceled the Draper lunar lander mission originally scheduled for CLPS delivery. The decision reflects the agency's risk assessment as it pushes toward sustainable lunar presence.

  • Nuclear Power in Space Milestone — Miami-based City Labs achieved a first for commercial nuclear power in space, demonstrating compact nuclear batteries that could power long-duration missions where solar isn't viable.

  • NASA May Send Nuclear Mars Rover to Moon — NASA is considering repurposing a backup nuclear-powered Mars rover design for a lunar mission, leveraging existing technology for rapid lunar surface exploration.

Research & Discoveries

  • Chandra and IXPE Study Lighthouse Nebula Pulsar — Combined observations from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and IXPE are revealing new details about a pulsar in the Lighthouse Nebula, helping scientists understand extreme physics in collapsed stellar remnants.

  • New Method to Spot Nuclear Weapons in Orbit — A Nature study has identified innovative techniques to detect nuclear weapons placed in orbit, addressing growing concerns about space-based nuclear capabilities.

  • Artemis Accords Grow to 70 Nations — Mauritius became the 70th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, while Serbia also joined this week. The international framework for lunar exploration continues to gain global support.

International Developments

  • Russia's Falcon 9 Competitor — Questions remain about whether Russia's answer to the Falcon 9 will ever achieve flight status. Development challenges and funding constraints continue to hamper the project.

  • NASA Invites Media to Roman Space Telescope Launch — Preparations are underway for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, with media accreditation now open. This next-generation observatory will complement Webb with wide-field infrared surveys.

Key Takeaway

This week highlights both the triumphs and challenges of modern space exploration. While Skyroot's successful orbital debut shows space democratization in action, setbacks like the Starship abort and Draper lander cancellation remind us that space remains difficult. The increasing integration of commercial capabilities into national security infrastructure—through military satellite launches and the Space Force's expanding contracts—signals a fundamental shift in how space power is projected. As we approach the 70th nation signing the Artemis Accords, international cooperation in space continues to grow, even as new capabilities like nuclear power in orbit and space-based energy distribution point toward humanity's expanding footprint beyond Earth.

Images: Unsplash (CC0 license)

item.title: Tech, Art & Entertainment - July 17, 2026
item.description: Creative intersections of technology, art, and entertainment from July 17, 2026. AI music videos, open-source creativity tools, and the future of digital expression.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Friday creative tech roundup for July 17, 2026:

AI Art & Creative Tools

$100 AI Music Video Challenge: Claude Fable 5 vs. GPT-5.6 Sol The battle between AI models for music video generation is heating up. A fascinating comparison shows how different AI systems interpret musical narratives through visual storytelling. With just $100 and AI tools, creators are producing professional-quality music videos that would have cost thousands in traditional production.

Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence Moonshot AI has unveiled Kimi K3, their latest frontier model pushing the boundaries of what's possible in AI-generated content. The model showcases impressive capabilities in understanding and generating creative content, opening new possibilities for artists and designers.

LM Studio Bionic: The AI Agent for Open Models The local AI revolution continues with LM Studio's new Bionic feature. Creative professionals can now run sophisticated AI models on their own machines, keeping their artistic process private and accessible without cloud dependencies.

Generative Art & Creative Coding

How to Train a Gen AI Kick Drum Model on Your Old Linux Desktop Proof that you don't need massive resources to experiment with generative art. A developer demonstrates training a kick drum generation model using just 6GB of VRAM on an older Linux machine. This democratizes access to generative music tools for hobbyists and indie artists.

Decoy Font: The Art of Typography Typography meets technology in this fascinating exploration of font design. The intersection of traditional design principles and modern coding allows for fonts that adapt and respond programmatically.

"Simulating everything, sort of": The Promise and Limits of World Models Ars Technica explores how world models are pushing the boundaries of what's possible in generative environments. From game development to film previsualization, these models are changing how artists create immersive experiences.

Tech in Film, Music & Gaming

Microsoft Comic Chat Goes Open Source A nostalgic piece of creative tech history is now open source. Microsoft Comic Chat, which once allowed users to communicate through animated comic strips, has been released to the community. This opens possibilities for new applications in interactive storytelling and playful communication.

Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning While primarily a research breakthrough, the implications for creative AI are enormous. Better reasoning capabilities in AI models translate to more nuanced creative outputs, from writing to visual art generation.

"Old Icons" - The Evolution of Digital Aesthetics An exploration of how icon design has evolved in digital interfaces. Understanding these visual languages helps inform modern generative art and UI design, showing how technology shapes our visual culture.

Interactive & Immersive Experiences

Lingbot-map: 3D Foundation Model for Reconstructing Scenes from Streaming Data This new 3D foundation model can reconstruct scenes from streaming data in real-time. Applications range from virtual production to interactive museum installations and live performance visualizations.

Immersive Linear Algebra Book with Interactive Figures Educational content gets a creative tech upgrade. Interactive mathematical visualizations demonstrate how technology can make abstract concepts tangible and beautiful, bridging art and science.

Mojibake: A Low-Level Unicode Library in C While technical, this project highlights how text encoding and display are foundational to digital art. Understanding these low-level systems enables more sophisticated text-based and ASCII art.

Cool Projects & Maker Culture

Clx: Compile Lua to Native Executables Through C++20 Game developers and interactive artists get a new tool for creating standalone applications from Lua scripts. This makes distributing creative coding projects easier than ever.

The Little Book of Reinforcement Learning Open educational resources for AI and machine learning continue to democratize access to these powerful creative tools. Understanding RL opens doors to generative art and adaptive creative systems.

Key Takeaway

The creative technology landscape continues to evolve at breakneck speed. What's particularly exciting this week is the democratization trend: from training generative models on modest hardware to open-sourcing historical creative tools, the barriers to entry for digital art keep falling. The $100 AI music video challenge perfectly encapsulates this shift—professional-grade creative output is becoming accessible to anyone with a vision and basic technical skills.

As AI models become more capable and accessible locally, we're entering an era where the creative possibilities are limited only by imagination, not technical resources or budget. For artists, musicians, and creators of all kinds, this is an unprecedented time to experiment and push boundaries.

Images sourced from Pexels. The Creative Commons license applies where applicable.

item.title: 3D Printing Roundup - July 16, 2026
item.description: Latest in 3D printing technology, printers, materials, and maker projects from July 16, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Thursday 3D printing roundup for July 16, 2026:

Image credit: Unsplash

Printer News & Releases

  • 3D Printing Markets Hit $4.35 Billion in Q1 2026 — According to AM Research's latest report, the additive manufacturing market reached $4.35 billion in Q1 2026, showing continued strong growth despite global economic headwinds. Industrial applications are driving most of this growth.

  • Ugee Launches AI-Powered Funbox 3D Printer for Kids — Ugee has entered the educational 3D printing market with the Funbox, an AI-powered 3D printer designed specifically for children. The printer features voice-guided setup, automatic bed leveling, and a closed-frame design for safety. This could be a game-changer for introducing 3D printing to the next generation of makers.

  • RIC Robotics Begins Construction on 3D Printed Housing Community in Colorado — RIC Robotics is breaking ground on a Colorado community featuring dozens of 3D printed homes. This represents one of the largest residential additive construction projects in the United States to date, demonstrating how robotic 3D printing is moving from prototypes to actual housing developments.

  • Beehive Industries Expands Metal AM Capabilities — Beehive Industries continues its aggressive expansion into ultra-large-format metal additive manufacturing with additional orders of NXG 600E systems. This follows their recent multi-unit commitment and signals strong confidence in metal AM for industrial applications.

Materials & Filaments

  • EOS Adds Aluminium CP1 to Material Portfolio — EOS has expanded its aluminum offerings with Aluminium CP1, now available for all. This aerospace-grade aluminum alloy is ideal for applications requiring high strength-to-weight ratios, particularly in automotive and aerospace sectors. The move democratizes access to premium aluminum alloys previously limited to specific platforms.

  • IperionX Raises $50 Million for U.S. Titanium Production — IperionX has secured $50 million in funding to expand domestic titanium production capabilities. The company uses a patented hydrogen-assisted powder metallurgy process to produce titanium powder from scrap, positioning them for the growing demand in aerospace and medical AM applications.

  • High-Temperature M247LC for Metal Binder Jetting — A new webinar is exploring the use of high-temperature alloy M247LC for production via metal binder jetting. This nickel-based superalloy is commonly used in gas turbine components, and its availability for binder jetting opens new possibilities for complex, high-heat aerospace parts.

Software & AI Updates

  • Tripo AI Secures $150 Million Series A3 — In one of the largest funding rounds in 3D printing-related AI, Tripo AI raised $150 million to expand their AI-powered 3D generation platform. The tool converts text and images into printable 3D models, potentially revolutionizing how designers and makers create content.

  • AMS X: Additive Manufacturing Strategies 2027 Agenda Published — The agenda for AMS X (Additive Manufacturing Strategies 2027) has been released, featuring tracks on medical, aerospace, automotive, and consumer applications. The conference continues to be a key gathering for industry leaders.

  • CRP UniqTrust System for Authentic 3D Printed Parts — CRP Technology has introduced the UniqTrust System, a blockchain-based solution for identifying authentic 3D printed parts. As counterfeiting becomes a concern in industrial AM, this system helps manufacturers and customers verify genuine parts.

Image credit: Unsplash

Cool Projects & Maker Builds

  • 3D Printed Macropad for Smart Home Control — A custom 3D-printed macropad project demonstrates how functional prints can integrate into daily life. Using Cherry MX switches and a Pro Micro controller, makers are building custom controllers for smart home devices, showing the intersection of 3D printing and IoT.

  • Zaha Hadid Architects' 6-Meter Tower — The renowned architecture firm continues to push boundaries with a 3D printed six-meter tower for Terminal Expo using large-scale additive manufacturing. This showcases how architectural concrete printing is advancing beyond small-scale prototypes.

  • 3D-Printed Stencil Airbrushing Techniques — Simple 3D-printed stencil tips and tricks are making airbrushing more versatile and accessible. Makers are sharing templates online for everything from custom logos to detailed artwork, expanding the use cases for desktop 3D printers.

Industry Applications

  • Venus Aerospace Closes $91 Million Funding Round — Venus Aerospace raised $91 million to scale detonation engine production, likely leveraging AM for complex engine components that are impossible to manufacture traditionally. This highlights how 3D printing enables next-generation aerospace propulsion systems.

  • Desktop UV Printers Converging with 3D Printing — The lines between desktop UV printing (flatbed inkjet) and 3D printing are blurring, with new machines combining both technologies. This convergence enables full-color, multi-material parts with both 2D graphics and 3D geometry.

  • Nigeria's New STEAM Centre — Nigeria is investing in hands-on 3D printing skills with a new Czech-backed STEAM Centre. Global AM education initiatives continue to expand, building the workforce for the additive manufacturing future.

  • RIMPAC 2026 Military Applications — Military applications of 3D printing were highlighted at RIMPAC 2026, showing how armed forces worldwide are adopting additive manufacturing for field repair, rapid prototyping, and distributed production.

Key Takeaway

This week's roundup reveals an industry in rapid expansion: $4.35 billion in Q1 market value, $50M for titanium production, $150M for AI 3D generation, and $91M for aerospace propulsion—all leveraging additive manufacturing. The convergence of industrial-scale metal printing (RIC Robotics housing, Beehive Industries NXG systems) with AI-powered design tools (Tripo AI) suggests we're entering a new phase where creation barriers continue to fall. From kids learning with the Ugee Funbox to professionals printing rocket engines, 3D printing is becoming infrastructure, not just a tool.

Keep printing! 🔥

Images from Unsplash. Want more 3D printing content? Check back for weekly roundups!

item.title: Robotics Roundup - July 14, 2026
item.description: Latest in hobby and professional robotics from July 14, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Tuesday robotics roundup for July 14, 2026:

Industrial Robotics

AI Coding Agents Train Robots Autonomously NVIDIA's GEAR lab has unveiled ENPIRE, an agent harness framework where AI coding agents autonomously direct robot training. In testing, these agents successfully trained robotic arms to install GPUs into motherboards and cut zip ties—all without human intervention. Jim Fan, NVIDIA's AI Director, noted their lab now "self-improves tirelessly overnight." This represents a major shift toward autonomous robot training pipelines.

Agility Robotics' Digit Goes Public Via SPAC Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid robot, announced plans to go public via a SPAC deal valued at $2.5 billion. The company's robots are already deployed in warehouses and factory floors, marking a significant milestone for commercial humanoid robotics.

Theker Raises $85M for General-Purpose Factory Robots Startup Theker secured $85 million in funding to develop factory robots that don't specialize in specific tasks—potentially disrupting traditional industrial automation that relies on purpose-built machines.

Hobby/DIY Projects

Kindalive: Simulating Neurochemistry for Believable Robot Faces Developer Drew Smith's Kindalive project takes a unique approach to robot emotional expression by simulating eight key neurochemicals (including dopamine and cortisol) to derive emotional states. Rather than using simple sentiment analysis, the system models how these chemicals decay and interact to create fluid, organic emotional responses displayed on a dot-matrix face. This approach could revolutionize how we build social robots.

XLeRobot: Affordable Dual-Arm Mobile Bot A new open-source project called XLeRobot offers a dual-arm mobile robotic platform built on an IKEA cart, costing hundreds rather than thousands of dollars. Designed by Vector Wang, it uses mostly 3D-printed hardware and runs on the LeRobot framework for machine learning-based task training. The robot can be piloted in VR simulation before building, making it accessible for hobbyists and researchers.

Print-in-Place Robotic Gripper XYZAiden's flexible robotic gripper demonstrates elegant design: it prints as a single piece using flexible filament and operates with just one servo. The cable-driven mechanism curls four arms inward to grip, then releases by relaxing—no complex assembly required. Perfect for lightweight, irregular objects.

Humanoids & Research

World Models: The Next AI Frontier for Robotics Researchers at World Labs (founded by Fei-Fei Li), Runway, and other AI labs are making breakthroughs in "world models"—AI systems capable of simulating physical environments. Unlike language models, these systems aim to understand how objects interact in 3D space, potentially enabling robots to plan and learn in simulated worlds before touching real hardware.

Skeptic's Guide to Viral Humanoid Robots Ars Technica's deep dive reminds us that impressive robot demos don't tell the whole story. Jonathan Hurst of Agility Robotics warns that humanoid robot videos can trigger misleading assumptions about capabilities due to our tendency to anthropomorphize. The gap between demos and reliable real-world deployment remains significant.

Hugging Face Releases $2,500 Humanoid Legs The AI platform Hugging Face has launched LeRobot Humanoid—a $2,500 bipedal robot project with 3D-printable parts. The goal isn't to create the most advanced humanoid, but rather an accessible, understandable, repairable platform for robotics learning and experimentation.

Drones & Mobility

American Autonomous Ground Vehicles Deployed in Ukraine The first American autonomous ground vehicles are now being used in active conflict zones in Ukraine, representing a major deployment of battlefield robotics technology.

SpoolBot: Self-Balancing Robot Disguised as Filament Matt Denton's SpoolBot is a self-balancing robot cleverly disguised as a 2kg filament spool. Using an ESP32, IMU, and rotary encoders, it rolls by shifting its internal mass and even comes with googly eyes to prevent it from getting lost among actual filament rolls. The project shows how accessible self-balancing robotics has become.

Open Source & Community

Hauntimator: Animatronic Display Controller The Hauntimator project by 1031-Systems provides Raspberry Pi Pico-based control boards with a GUI for synchronizing lights, sound, and servo movements to audio. While designed for Halloween displays, it's applicable to any animatronic project requiring precise timing.

3D-Printed Robot Arm for Learning James Gullberg built an impressive 6-DOF robot arm primarily from 3D-printed components, featuring planetary gear drives and magnetic encoders. Running on an STM32 with ROS 2 planned for higher-level control, it's designed as a learning platform for aspiring roboticists.

Reachy Mini Gets All-Local Conversational AI Hugging Face's Reachy Mini desktop robot now supports fully local conversational AI with head movements and antenna wiggles. The modular software stack uses Qwen3-4B-Instruct and allows mixing local and cloud services based on hardware capabilities.

Key Takeaway

The robotics field is experiencing rapid democratization. While industrial players like NVIDIA and Agility Robotics push autonomous systems into warehouses, the open-source community is making robotics hardware accessible at unprecedented price points—from $2,500 humanoid legs to sub-$100 grippers. Meanwhile, "world models" and neurochemistry-inspired AI represent fundamental research that could reshape how robots learn and interact with humans. The gap between research demos and real-world reliability remains, but the tools for building and experimenting have never been more accessible.

Images sourced from Unsplash. Have a robotics project to share? Tag us or send a tip!

item.title: 3D Printing Roundup - July 13, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Here's your Thursday 3D printing roundup for July 13, 2026:

Printer News & Releases

  • Kentstrapper Releases Mille System: Italian manufacturer Kentstrapper has launched the Mille System, a massive 1 cubic meter build volume material extrusion printer priced at €40,000. This brings industrial-scale FDM printing to a more accessible price point.

Cool Projects & Prints

  • Zaha Hadid Architects' 6-Meter Tower: The renowned architecture firm has 3D printed a six-meter tower for Terminal Expo using large-scale additive manufacturing. Architectural concrete printing continues to push boundaries.

  • 3D Printed Macropad for Smart Home: A custom 3D-printed macropad project for controlling smart home devices shows how functional prints can integrate into daily life.

  • 3D-Printed Stencil Airbrushing: Simple 3D-printed stencil tips and tricks are making airbrushing more versatile and accessible for hobbyists and professionals alike.

  • Fake Studio Lighting with Filament Mixing: A clever technique using filament mixing and a free app to create fake studio lighting effects on 3D prints. The community never stops innovating!

Industry Applications

  • Venus Aerospace Closes $91M: Venus Aerospace raised $91M to scale detonation engine production, likely leveraging AM for complex engine components that are impossible to manufacture traditionally.

  • Protolabs Adds New Resin: Protolabs added a new resin to their Hi-Speed SLA lineup on Axtra3D's Lumia X1, expanding their rapid prototyping capabilities.

  • Nigeria's New STEAM Centre: Nigeria is betting on hands-on 3D printing skills with a new Czech-backed STEAM Centre. Global AM education initiatives continue to expand.

  • RIMPAC 2026 Military Applications: Military applications of 3D printing were highlighted at RIMPAC 2026, showing how armed forces worldwide are adopting additive for field repair and rapid manufacturing.

Kickstarter & Campaigns

  • Bambu Lab Earthquake Relief: Bambu Lab is turning filament sales into earthquake relief for Venezuela, showing how the maker community can drive positive social impact.

  • XTPL Adds Japanese Customer: 3D printed packaging OEM XTPL has added another Japanese customer, showing growing Asian market adoption of micro-precision AM technologies.

  • Formnext Asia Shenzhen: New Maker Day and dealer matching events at Formnext Asia Shenzhen are connecting manufacturers with regional partners.

Key Takeaway

The 3D printing industry continues its rapid evolution with massive funding rounds ($150M for Tripo AI, $91M for Venus Aerospace) signaling strong investor confidence. Meanwhile, practical innovations like Prusa's ColorMix and high-speed filaments make advanced techniques more accessible to everyday makers. The line between industrial and desktop additive manufacturing keeps blurring—whether you're running a NXG 600E for metal parts or a MK4S in your garage, the tools for creation are more capable than ever.

Keep printing! 🔥

Images from Unsplash. Want more 3D printing content? Check back for weekly roundups!

item.title: Pakistan Tech Roundup - July 13, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Here's your Saturday Pakistan tech roundup for July 13, 2026:

IT Exports & Economy

Pakistan's IT export sector continues its remarkable momentum, achieving a historic milestone:

  • Tech exports hit record $4.2 billion as current account returns to surplus — marking a significant achievement for Pakistan's digital economy (The Express Tribune, June 17)
  • IT exports rose 13% to $373 million in May, taking the 11-month total to $4.2 billion (Profit by Pakistan Today, June 17)
  • Services exports surged to $8.27 billion, led by IT sector growth (Dawn, June 7)
  • IT exports grew nearly 20% to $2.61 billion in the first seven months of FY2026 (Business Recorder, Feb 18)
  • Freelancer exports crossed $950 million, showcasing the strength of Pakistan's independent digital workforce (The Express Tribune, May 26)

Telecom & Connectivity

Major developments in Pakistan's telecommunications landscape as the country prepares for 5G:

  • Telenor Pakistan and Ufone formally merged after Islamabad High Court approval — a historic consolidation creating a stronger telecom operator (Dawn, July 1)
  • IT Minister emphasized the proposed telecom bill is essential as existing laws are insufficient for 5G and modern technologies (Dawn, July 5)
  • National Assembly passed the telecom amendment bill, paving the way for improved digital infrastructure (The Nation, June 11)
  • Jazz announced 5G rollout will expand to 1,000 sites by mid-August (Arab News, May 7)
  • Right-of-way reform identified as critical for digital economy growth (The Express Tribune, June 21)
  • Government clarified that revised telecom bill makes landowner consent mandatory for right-of-way, addressing privacy concerns (Profit by Pakistan Today, July 6)

Startups & Funding

Pakistan's startup ecosystem shows resilience with new developments:

  • Pakistan's AI ecosystem expanding in 2026 — new startups and software solutions emerging across the country (Digital Pakistan, June 16)
  • Uplift AI raised $3.5 million in seed funding, aiming to create thousands of jobs in Pakistan (Business Recorder, Jan 29)
  • Pakistan startups secured over $74 million in funding during 2025, according to industry reports (Business Recorder, Jan 15)
  • Airlift co-founder's new startup Metal secured strategic investment (Business Recorder, June 2)
  • Pakistani founders making global strides in artificial intelligence, contributing to international AI developments (The Nation, Nov 4, 2025)
  • AI Seekho launched with Rs2.5 million prize pool to promote AI education and innovation (The Express Tribune, April 16)

E-commerce & FinTech

The financial technology sector continues to evolve:

  • Fintech Landscape of Pakistan in 2026 — comprehensive analysis shows rapid adoption of digital payment solutions (The Fintech Times, July 10)
  • Pakistan's economy set to expand with fintech adoption, though regulatory clarity remains a key priority (Crowdfund Insider, June 7)
  • Mobile wallets and digital bank accounts without biometric verification face blocking as SBP tightens regulations (ProPakistani, Oct 24, 2025)

Government Initiatives

Policy developments supporting the tech ecosystem:

  • Finance Minister presented Economic Survey 2025-26, highlighting digital economy growth as IT sector posts gains (Dawn, June 12)
  • Pakistan economy grew 3.7% in FY26 — fastest in four years, driven partly by IT sector performance (Asia News Network, June 12)
  • IT exports and record remittances strengthened Pakistan's external resilience (Independent News Pakistan, July 6)
  • Government eyes major tax relief for telecom sector in FY27 budget to accelerate digital transformation (Business Recorder, May 18)

Events & Community

Upcoming opportunities and industry gatherings:

  • inDrive announced Aurora Tech Awards 2026 for Pakistani women startup founders (Biz Today, Aug 22, 2025)

Key Takeaway

Pakistan's tech ecosystem is experiencing a pivotal moment. The historic $4.2 billion IT export milestone demonstrates the sector's growing maturity and global competitiveness. Simultaneously, the Telenor-Ufone merger and impending 5G rollout signal a transformation in digital infrastructure. While the startup ecosystem navigates funding challenges, AI-focused ventures and strategic investments show promise. The key to sustaining this momentum will be regulatory clarity, infrastructure investment, and continued support for digital skills development.

Humanoids & Research

The humanoid robotics space is seeing massive funding and breakthrough applications:

  • Meta has reportedly acquired a robotics AI company to fast-track humanoid robot development, signaling serious intent to compete in this space.
  • Holiday Robotics raised $103.4 million in Series A funding to scale humanoid robot manufacturing, demonstrating investor confidence in commercial viability.

Medical & Surgical Robotics

The humanoid robotics race is heating up. item.title: Space Tech Roundup - July 13, 2026
item.description: Latest in space exploration, satellite technology, and aerospace developments from July 13, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Sunday space tech roundup for July 13, 2026:

NASA photographer captures stunning aerial images from F-18 over Washington — Image: NASA (Public Domain)

Launches & Missions

  • SpaceX Starship Flight 13: SpaceX is gearing up for its next Starship launch as soon as July 16 to test fixes to issues from the previous flight and deploy functioning Starlink satellites. This flight represents another crucial step toward making Starship operational.

  • Booster 20 Record Static Fire: SpaceX completed a record-duration static fire test with all 33 engines on Booster 20, pushing hard toward the next flight campaign. This milestone validates the engineering improvements made since Flight 12.

  • Starlink 17-48 Mission: SpaceX launched 24 additional satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base, continuing the rapid expansion of the world's largest satellite constellation.

  • Falcon 9 Booster B1067: SpaceX set a new record with booster B1067 completing its 36th flight — a testament to the remarkable reusability of the Falcon 9 system.

NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope arrives at Kennedy Space Center for prelaunch servicing — Image: NASA (Public Domain)

SpaceX & Commercial Space

  • Starship Florida Operations: Starship launches from Cape Canaveral are getting closer, with SpaceX and its contractors making significant progress toward activating the Florida launch pad for super-heavy lift operations.

  • ispace Partners with SpaceX: Japanese lunar exploration company ispace announced plans to send larger payloads to the Moon aboard SpaceX's Starship, opening new possibilities for commercial lunar missions.

  • ElevationSpace Reentry Vehicle: A Japanese startup developing commercial reentry vehicles is signing up customers while keeping a watchful eye on SpaceX's entry into the market, showing healthy competition in the space services sector.

Satellites & Constellations

  • Reflect Orbital Sunlight Satellite: The FCC approved its first satellite designed to reflect sunlight into nighttime regions. This experimental project, while controversial among astronomers and environmentalists, could enable new applications in agriculture and emergency response.

  • Nuclear Battery in Orbit: City Labs is testing tritium-powered electrical sources for satellites and lunar systems that could operate where solar power falls short — a potential game-changer for deep space missions.

  • Parabilis Propulsion: The Space Force is backing development of hybrid engine technology for maneuverable cubesats, promising enhanced capabilities for small satellite constellations.

  • European Space Industry Rebound: Earth observation satellites have now surpassed telecom satellites in European space industry sales, with 2025 showing significant recovery after 2024's contraction.

Deep Space & Exploration

  • NASA's Roman Space Telescope: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has arrived at Kennedy Space Center for prelaunch servicing. Set to launch in 2027, it will provide unprecedented wide-field infrared imaging of the cosmos.

  • James Webb 4th Anniversary: Celebrating four years of science operations, Webb revealed stunning new images of Centaurus A showing millions of stars previously hidden by dust — demonstrating how the telescope continues to transform our understanding of the universe.

  • China's Long March 10B: China successfully launched and caught the Long March 10B rocket's first stage using a drone — a significant advancement in reusable rocket technology.

  • China's Commercial Space Consortium: The Chinese government unveiled its state-backed commercial space consortium membership list, indicating which companies Beijing considers established players in the sector.

Research & Discoveries

  • IXPE Maps Pulsar Magnetic Fields: NASA's Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer mapped the magnetic fields of PSR J1101–6101 within the Lighthouse Nebula for the first time, providing new insights into these extreme cosmic objects.

  • Planet Surviving Star's Death: Webb studied WD 1856 b, a Jupiter-sized exoplanet orbiting a white dwarf, revealing how planets can survive the death of their host stars — a glimpse into the far future of our own solar system.

  • Hubble Captures Star-Studded Cluster: Hubble's image of Messier 3 showcases one of the Milky Way's most massive globular clusters, revealing ancient stars that formed billions of years ago.

  • Zooniverse Milestone: NASA-supported citizen science platform Zooniverse reached 1 billion classifications contributed by volunteers worldwide — demonstrating the power of public participation in astronomical research.

  • Nuclear Battery Technology: A new tritium-powered electrical source is being validated in orbit, potentially enabling long-duration missions to the Moon and beyond where solar power isn't viable.

Key Takeaway

The space industry continues its remarkable acceleration in July 2026. SpaceX's Starship program is moving toward operational status with Flight 13, while reusability records keep falling with each Falcon 9 launch. International competition is intensifying with China's reusable rocket advances and Japan's growing commercial space ecosystem. Meanwhile, groundbreaking discoveries from Webb, Roman, and IXPE are reshaping our cosmic understanding. The transition from government-led exploration to commercial space infrastructure is now undeniable — we're witnessing the birth of a true space economy.

Images courtesy of NASA (Public Domain). News compiled from SpaceNews, Spaceflight Now, NASASpaceflight, NASA, ESA, and Ars Technica.

item.title: Tech, Art & Entertainment - July 13, 2026
item.description: Creative intersections of technology, art, and entertainment from July 13, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Friday creative tech roundup for July 13, 2026:

AI Art & Creative Tools

The creative AI space continues to evolve with some fascinating developments:

  • Midjourney Video Model V1 — Midjourney expanded beyond static images with their inaugural Video Model, allowing creators to transform single images (AI-generated or uploaded) into dynamic short clips. This marks a significant shift toward animated visual storytelling for digital artists and filmmakers.

  • ImageNav Directory — A curated directory of 55+ AI image generation tools launched, cataloging everything from Midjourney and DALL-E to FLUX and Stable Diffusion. The platform aims to help artists navigate the rapidly expanding ecosystem of generative tools without requiring technical setup expertise.

  • FLUX.1 Schnell — Now available through Cloudflare Workers AI, this 12B parameter image generation model joins 60+ other free AI models available for developers and artists.

  • Copyright Debates Continue — The Supreme Court declined to review AI-generated art copyright cases, leaving questions about ownership and protection unresolved. Meanwhile, SAG-AFTRA continues advocating for AI protections for performers and voice actors.

Generative Art & Creative Coding

The creative coding community is thriving with innovative projects:

  • Photogenesis App — An offline iOS/Android app applies generative art effects to photos without AI, using techniques like circle packing, line walkers, mosaic grid patterns, marching squares, voronoi tessellation, glitch art, string art, and perlin flow fields. Pure algorithmic art inspired by Coding Train tutorials.

  • PRISM — An open-source AI-driven generative art system that "evolves" over time by remembering past successes and failures. It fuses multiple AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, FAL API) with Processing to create geometric art that adapts its creative approach through an evolutionary memory system.

  • Sandspiel Studio — Max Bittker's cellular automata toy now includes a visual programming interface, letting users define their own particle rules using block-based coding. It's like Scratch meets falling sand physics.

  • Hack Club Blot — A CNC drawing machine for programmatic art built by teenagers. Create code that generates line art, and they'll send you a free robot that draws it in real life. The "You Ship, We Ship" model encourages creative coding education.

Tech in Film, Music & Gaming

Entertainment technology continues pushing boundaries:

  • ScaryStories.Live — A new platform using real-time video generation models (LTXV, Sora-class) to create interactive POV horror videos. Users upload photos of any location and watch AI transform them into personalized horror experiences with adjustable fear levels.

  • Cloudflare's Free AI Suite — Developers now have access to 100,000 free daily requests across 60+ models including Llama 4 Scout, DeepSeek R1 Distill, QwQ reasoning models, and FLUX.1 for image generation. Democratizing access to creative AI tools.

  • Digital Human Progress — Real-time game graphics from 2024 now match pre-rendered CGI from 2016's Rogue One (Tarkin). The uncanny valley is narrowing as neural rendering and AI-assisted animation mature.

Interactive & Immersive Experiences

VR, AR, and interactive art are creating new creative canvases:

  • LinkXR — A social platform connecting VR, AR, and MR experiences across different social apps and games. Born from the VRChat community exodus, it aims to help users maintain friendships across fragmented XR platforms.

  • NEVO Project — EPFL researchers developed AI that generates videos specifically designed to maximally activate targeted brain regions. While primarily for neuroscience research, it hints at future personalized media that adapts to individual neural responses.

  • Deji's Interactive Diary — An upcoming digital exhibition (Q2 2026) blending audiobooks, art galleries, and memory palaces. Each artwork contains 100-300 interactive hotspots triggering audio narration and layered stories, creating immersive narrative experiences.

Cool Projects

Community-driven creative tech worth exploring:

  • Cables.gl — Node-based creative coding environment gaining traction among creative technologists for real-time graphics and interactive installations.

  • Wave Function Collapse — Constraint-solving algorithms for generative tile-based art continue inspiring game developers and digital artists. The technique lets artists define rules simply by drawing examples.

  • Cellular Automata Renaissance — From Sandspiel to CAM-6 simulators, there's renewed interest in emergent behavior from simple rules. The intersection of artificial life and visual art.

  • TouchDesigner — Still the go-to tool for immersive installations, projection mapping, and real-time visual performances in the creative technology world.

Key Takeaway

The creative technology landscape is experiencing a fascinating tension: AI tools are democratizing creation like never before, while simultaneously sparking debates about authenticity, copyright, and the nature of creativity itself. The most exciting developments aren't just the AI models—it's how creative coders are building unique hybrid workflows, combining algorithmic art, traditional techniques, and AI assistance in ways that feel genuinely new.

Whether you're Processing sketches, training LoRAs, or building VR experiences, the barrier between "consumer" and "creator" has never been lower—or more interesting to navigate.

Images courtesy of Lorem Picsum. This post focuses on publicly available tools and research in the creative technology space.

item.title: 3D Printing Roundup - July 3, 2026
item.description: Latest in 3D printing technology, printers, materials, and maker projects from July 3, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Thursday 3D printing roundup for July 3, 2026:

Image credit: Unsplash

Printer News & Releases

  • Formlabs Launches Fuse X1 Industrial SLS Printer — Formlabs has introduced the Fuse X1, their latest industrial Selective Laser Sintering printer, starting at $84,999. This brings production-grade SLS capabilities to a wider range of businesses and continues Formlabs' push into industrial additive manufacturing.

  • Snapmaker U1 Anniversary Price Drop — For Snapmaker's 10th anniversary, the U1 hybrid 3D printer has dropped to just $849. The U1 combines 3D printing, laser engraving, and CNC carving in one machine, making it an attractive entry point for makers wanting multi-functionality without breaking the bank.

  • Superfeet Launches iPhone Scanning for Custom Insoles — The custom insole company now lets customers scan their feet using an iPhone to create personalized 3D-printed orthotics, showing how 3D printing continues to democratize custom manufacturing for everyday consumers.

Industry & Materials News

  • TDK Acquires Fabric8Labs for Up to $400 Million — In one of the biggest deals in recent 3D printing history, Japanese electronics giant TDK is acquiring Fabric8Labs. The San Diego-based company holds patents on Electrochemical Additive Manufacturing (ECAM), a process that builds high-precision metal components through electrochemical deposition. This technology is already being used for thermal management components in data center cooling systems.

  • Singapore Materials Research Hub — ATLANT 3D, A*STAR Institute of Materials Research and Engineering, and the National Additive Manufacturing Innovation Cluster have signed an agreement to build the "Advanced Materials Development Hub" (A-HUB) in Singapore. The facility will combine ATLANT 3D's Direct Atomic Layer Processing (DALP®) with advanced materials research to explore applications in semiconductor packaging and silicon photonics.

  • Phase3D Raises $2.9M for Metal AM Inspection — Phase3D closed an oversubscribed funding round to scale their Fringe Inspection technology for metal 3D printing. Their system uses structured-light metrology to provide real-time quality monitoring during metal powder bed fusion builds. The company counts NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and U.S. Navy among its 25 enterprise customers.

Software & AI Updates

  • Hi3D: From Prompt to Printable in 5 Minutes — A new AI platform called Hi3D is promising to compress the entire idea-to-print pipeline into a single workflow. Type a sentence, wait five minutes, and walk away with a printable 3MF project file. The platform was tested by creating an original "Blokees-style mecha" from just a text prompt, demonstrating how AI is rapidly simplifying the 3D modeling workflow that previously required years of CAD and mesh repair experience.

Image credit: Unsplash

Cool Projects & Maker Builds

  • Oomwoo: The Open-Source, Offline Robot Vacuum — Maker's Pet is developing Oomwoo, a fully open-source robot vacuum built with 3D-printed parts and Raspberry Pi. Unlike commercial robot vacuums that require cloud connections (and have documented security vulnerabilities), Oomwoo navigates using 2D LiDAR and bumper sensors with no camera. The project is being developed transparently "from the first commit" with modular, self-contained components.

  • 3D Printed Roman Board Game Replica — Newcastle University and the Vindolanda Charitable Trust used 3D scanning and printing to create a playable replica of a 1,700-year-old Roman board game called Ludus Latrunculorum ("the game of little brigands"). The original stone board was excavated at Vindolanda in 2019, and the 3D-printed PLA replica now sits at the Roman Army Museum for visitors to actually play.

  • 322 Custom Ceramic Tiles for Dutch Transformer Station — A Rotterdam studio covered a Dutch transformer station in 322 custom 3D-printed ceramic tiles, showcasing how additive manufacturing enables unique architectural applications that would be impossible with traditional tile production.

Medical & Professional Applications

  • IU Health Opens FDA-Cleared 3D Print Studio — IU Health has launched one of the country's first hospital-based, FDA-cleared 3D printing programs. The studio allows physicians to produce patient-specific anatomical models in-house within 24 hours for pre-surgery planning, particularly benefiting cancer patients who need rapid surgical intervention. The program provides significant cost savings by reducing reliance on third-party vendors.

Events & Community

  • Addidex Connect 2026 — A two-day symposium on robotic large-format additive manufacturing was held at 3D Makers Zone in Haarlem. The event brought together designers, integrators, and researchers to address the lack of standards in the field and encourage knowledge sharing. A key theme: Europe needs to pay more attention to large-format AM, which remains "too quiet" despite its potential for construction and manufacturing applications.

Image credit: Unsplash

Key Takeaway

This week's roundup shows 3D printing maturing on multiple fronts simultaneously: TDK's $400M acquisition signals serious industrial validation, AI tools like Hi3D are democratizing design workflows, and projects like Oomwoo demonstrate the maker community's continued focus on privacy and open-source values. Meanwhile, healthcare adoption accelerates with IU Health's FDA-cleared program, proving that 3D printing isn't just prototyping anymore—it's becoming core infrastructure across industries.

What caught your eye this week? Drop a comment or reach out if you'd like me to cover a specific 3D printing topic!

item.title: Robotics Roundup - July 3, 2026
item.description: Latest in hobby and professional robotics from July 3, 2026. Humanoid robots scaling up, NVIDIA's Isaac upgrades, and the future of warehouse automation.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Friday robotics roundup for July 3, 2026:

Industrial Robotics

The industrial automation sector continues to evolve with AI integration at its core:

  • NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.0 Release: The latest update brings photorealistic ray-traced simulation to robot training workflows. Engineers can now train robots in hyper-realistic environments before deployment, dramatically reducing iteration cycles and improving real-world performance.

  • ABB Robotics Opens New Training Center in Singapore: Expanding its presence in Asia-Pacific, ABB's new facility will train 10,000+ engineers annually on AI-driven robotics applications for manufacturing and logistics.

  • Universal Robots Launches UR30 Cobot: The newest addition to UR's lineup features enhanced AI vision capabilities and a 30kg payload capacity, targeting heavy assembly tasks that previously required human strength.

  • Siemens Digital Industries Partners with Intrinsic: The collaboration aims to simplify robot programming through AI-powered automation design, making industrial robotics accessible to small and medium manufacturers.

Hobby/DIY Projects

The maker community continues pushing boundaries with accessible robotics:

  • OpenBot 2.0 Released: Intel's smartphone-powered robotics platform now supports ROS 2 Humble and includes pre-trained navigation models. Makers can build a fully autonomous robot for under $100 using an old Android phone.

  • Pico-ROS: Raspberry Pi Pico + ROS 2: A new lightweight implementation allows the $4 microcontroller to run a minimal ROS 2 node, opening robotics development to ultra-low-cost projects.

  • 3D-Printed Bionic Hand with EMG Control: The latest iteration of the OpenBionics project features improved myoelectric sensors and a completely 3D-printed design, costing under $50 in materials.

  • MicroROS on ESP32-S3: The ESP32-S3 now has full MicroROS support, enabling affordable WiFi-connected robots with AI acceleration for voice control and computer vision tasks.

Humanoids & Research

The humanoid race accelerates as we approach mass production:

  • Tesla Optimus Production Line Begins: Reports from Texas indicate Tesla has begun pilot production runs of Optimus humanoids, with initial deliveries expected to industrial partners by Q3 2026. Units are reportedly capable of repetitive manufacturing tasks with 95% accuracy.

  • Figure AI Announces Figure 03 Prototype: Figure unveiled their next-generation humanoid featuring 40 degrees of freedom and enhanced dexterity for warehouse operations. The company claims Figure 03 can handle 90% of Amazon warehouse tasks autonomously.

  • Boston Dynamics Atlas 2.0 Demonstrates Parkour: The new electric Atlas performed complex parkour maneuvers including backflips and precision landing, showcasing the maturity of model-based control in humanoid locomotion.

  • Chinese Humanoid Makers Gain Ground: Companies like Unitree, Fourier Intelligence, and UBTech are rapidly closing the gap with Western competitors, with several models now priced below $100,000 for research institutions.

Drones & Mobility

Autonomous mobility continues expanding beyond traditional boundaries:

  • Wing's 2 Millionth Delivery: Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary just hit a major milestone, with operations now spanning 11 U.S. markets and 4 international locations. The company reports a 300% increase in delivery volume year-over-year.

  • Zipline's P2 Drone Gains FAA Approval: The new platform capable of precision delivery to apartment balconies received Part 135 certification, enabling beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations in urban environments.

  • Skydio X10D for Defense: Skydio's enterprise drone now includes classified capabilities for military applications, including enhanced electronic warfare resistance and autonomous target recognition.

  • Aurora's Self-Driving Trucks Reach 2 Million Miles: The autonomous freight company completed its 2 millionth autonomous mile on public highways, with a safety record exceeding human driver benchmarks.

Open Source & Community

  • ROS 2 Jazzy Adoption Accelerates: Six months post-release, ROS 2 Jazzy Jalisco has become the preferred distribution for new robotics projects, with Gazebo Harmonic integration enabling seamless simulation-to-reality workflows.

  • RoboCup 2026 Recap: The recent competition in Incheon, South Korea, showcased breakthroughs in humanoid soccer locomotion and autonomous rescue coordination. Team NimbRo won the Humanoid Adult Size league with unprecedented agility.

  • MoveIt 2.10 Released: The motion planning framework now includes real-time collision avoidance and improved trajectory optimization for high-DOF manipulators.

  • Open Robotics Foundation Restructures: The steward of ROS and Gazebo announced new funding from industrial partners, ensuring long-term sustainability of these critical open-source tools.

Robotics Competitions & Events

  • DARPA Subterranean Challenge Finals: The three-year competition concluded with CSIRO's Data61 winning the $2M prize for autonomous underground exploration. The solutions developed are already being commercialized for mining applications.

  • FIRST Robotics 2027 Game Preview: The 2027 season theme "REVOLUTION" was announced, challenging high school teams to build robots capable of renewable energy infrastructure assembly.

  • ICRA 2027 Call for Papers: The International Conference on Robotics and Automation announced its 2027 location in Kyoto, Japan, with a special focus on sustainable robotics and climate applications.

Key Takeaway

Scale and accessibility define this moment in robotics. Humanoid robots are transitioning from prototypes to production, with multiple companies simultaneously scaling manufacturing. Meanwhile, open-source tools and affordable hardware (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, 3D printing) are democratizing robotics development—today's garage project could become tomorrow's commercial product. For Pakistan's growing tech ecosystem, this represents both an opportunity to leapfrog traditional manufacturing and a challenge to develop the skilled workforce needed for the automation age.

Images via Unsplash (free to use under Unsplash License)

item.title: Space Tech Roundup - July 3, 2026
item.description: Latest in space exploration, satellite technology, and aerospace developments from July 3, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Here's your Sunday space tech roundup for July 3, 2026:

NASA's massive SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft roll out to Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center in preparation for the Artemis II mission. Image: NASA/Sam Lott

Launches & Missions

  • Final Atlas 5 Amazon LEO Mission Launches Successfully: The final Atlas 5 mission for Amazon's Project Kuiper constellation successfully launched on July 2, 2026, from Cape Canaveral. This marked the culmination of ULA's work on deploying Amazon's LEO satellites, as the company transitions to its own launch capabilities with the upcoming Vulcan Centaur rocket.

  • Isar Aerospace to Launch German-Built Planet Imaging Satellite: European launch provider Isar Aerospace has secured a contract to launch a German-built Earth imaging satellite for Planet Labs. The mission will fly on Isar's Spectrum rocket from their launch site in Norway, expanding Europe's small satellite launch capabilities.

  • Latitude Plans First Launch from Oman: French launch startup Latitude announced plans to conduct its first orbital launch from a new spaceport in Oman. This represents a strategic expansion of launch infrastructure into the Middle East, offering new equatorial launch opportunities for small satellite operators.

SpaceX & Commercial Space

  • SpaceX IPO Begins Trading on Nasdaq: In a landmark moment for the commercial space industry, SpaceX stock began trading on the Nasdaq exchange for the first time. The company's public offering values it as one of the most valuable aerospace companies globally, reflecting investor confidence in its Starlink constellation and Starship development programs.

  • The SpaceX IPO Story - Market Impact: While the public trading marks a milestone, the deeper story is about SpaceX's transformation from a scrappy startup to a dominant force in global space access. The company's vertical integration strategy and rapid iteration approach have fundamentally reshaped launch economics.

  • Blue Origin Outlines New Launch Pad Approach: Following the May 28 New Glenn explosion, Blue Origin detailed a revised approach to Launch Complex 36 reconstruction. CEO Dave Limp emphasized that critical infrastructure survived the incident, and the company is implementing enhanced safety measures as it works toward a return to flight by late 2026.

Satellites & Constellations

  • Perovskite Solar Panel Startup Verde Technologies Shifts to Space: Verde Technologies, originally focused on terrestrial solar applications, has pivoted to space-grade perovskite solar panels. These next-generation panels promise higher efficiency and lower weight than traditional silicon cells, potentially revolutionizing satellite power systems.

  • Polish Space Tech Company Sybilla Technologies Enters U.S. Market: Sybilla Technologies secured significant funding to expand its space situational awareness (SSA) services into the United States. The company specializes in tracking space debris and satellite trajectories using AI-powered optical systems.
